questions.stem: In a practice exercise, for a brass system with internal energy change 59 kJ and entropy change -54 J per K held at constant volume, compute the Helmholtz free energy change at 378 K in kJ.

options.misconception: Did not convert entropy units to kJ
Correct application of the principle
Added the T delta S term instead of subtracting
Ignored entropy and reported internal energy alone

questions.explanation: Helmholtz free energy is defined as A equals U minus T S, so its change at constant temperature is delta U minus T delta S. With entropy in J per K converted to kJ per K, the value at 378 K is 79.41 kJ; its decrease sets the maximum work obtainable at constant volume and temperature.
questions.hint: Delta A = delta U - T delta S.

questions.subject: THERMODYNAMICS
questions.learningObjective: Apply Maximum Non-Expansion Work principles to solve a quantitative thermodynamics problem.
questions.stem: In a practice exercise, an iron process at constant temperature and pressure has delta H 9 kJ and delta S -51 J per K at 355 K. Find the maximum non-expansion work in kJ.

options.misconception: Correct application of the principle
Used the negative of enthalpy instead of free energy
Used enthalpy change instead of free energy
Used delta G itself instead of its negative

questions.explanation: At constant temperature and pressure the maximum useful non-expansion work equals minus the change in Gibbs free energy. Computing delta G as delta H minus T delta S gives 27.11 kJ, so the maximum non-expansion work is -27.11 kJ; a negative delta G corresponds to positive work available.
questions.hint: Maximum non-PV work = -delta G.

questions.subject: THERMODYNAMICS
questions.learningObjective: Apply Otto Cycle Efficiency principles to solve a quantitative thermodynamics problem.
questions.stem: In a research run, with lead cylinder walls, compression ratio 12, and inlet temperature 287 K, an ideal Otto cycle at gamma 1.4 runs; compute its air-standard thermal efficiency as a percentage.

options.misconception: Used gamma instead of gamma minus one in the exponent
Correct application of the principle
Used a simple one minus reciprocal ratio expression
Reported the reciprocal term without subtracting it

questions.explanation: The ideal Otto efficiency is one minus one over the compression ratio raised to gamma minus one. With compression ratio 12 and gamma 1.4 the exponent is 0.4, giving 63.0 percent; raising the compression ratio increases efficiency but is limited by knock in real engines.
questions.hint: Otto efficiency = 1 - 1/r^(gamma - 1).

questions.stem: In a research run, with lead compressor blades, pressure ratio 4, and inlet temperature 285 K, an ideal Brayton cycle at gamma 1.4 runs; compute its thermal efficiency as a percentage.

options.misconception: Used gamma instead of (gamma minus one) over gamma
Flipped the sign of the pressure-ratio exponent
Correct application of the principle
Reported the pressure term itself without subtracting

questions.explanation: For an ideal Brayton cycle the efficiency depends on the pressure ratio as one minus rp raised to minus (gamma minus one) over gamma. With rp equal to 4 and gamma 1.4 this gives 32.7 percent; higher pressure ratios improve efficiency at the cost of heavier compressors.
questions.hint: Brayton efficiency = 1 - (1/rp)^((gamma-1)/gamma).

questions.subject: THERMODYNAMICS
questions.learningObjective: Apply Carnot Cycle Work principles to solve a quantitative thermodynamics problem.
questions.stem: In a research run, a brass Carnot engine working between 778 K and 284 K absorbs 911 J per cycle from the hot reservoir; calculate the work output per cycle in joules.

options.misconception: Correct application of the principle
Reported the full absorbed heat as work
Added the reservoir ratio to the absorbed heat
Computed the heat rejected rather than the work

questions.explanation: A reversible Carnot engine converts a fraction (1 minus Tc over Th) of the absorbed heat into work. With reservoirs at 778 K and 284 K and heat input 911 J, the work output is 578 J per cycle; the remainder is rejected to the cold reservoir.
questions.hint: Work = Q_in (1 - T_cold/T_hot) for a Carnot cycle.

questions.subject: THERMODYNAMICS
questions.learningObjective: Apply Compression-Ignition Cycle Efficiency principles to solve a quantitative thermodynamics problem.
questions.stem: In a calibration run, at compression ratio 15 and cutoff ratio 2.19 with gamma 1.4, an ideal compression-ignition cycle with silver pistons runs. Compute its air-standard efficiency as a percentage.

options.misconception: Correct application of the principle
Reported only the cutoff correction, not one minus it
Used gamma rather than gamma minus one
Used the Otto cycle formula and ignored the cutoff ratio

questions.explanation: The compression-ignition cycle efficiency equals one minus one over r to the gamma minus one times a cutoff-ratio factor (rho to the gamma minus one) over (gamma times rho minus one). With r 15 and rho 2.19 the efficiency is 59.4 percent; at a cutoff ratio of one it reduces to the Otto result.
questions.hint: Diesel-type efficiency = 1 - [1/r^(gamma-1)] [(rho^gamma - 1)/(gamma(rho - 1))].

questions.subject: THERMODYNAMICS
questions.learningObjective: Apply Rankine Cycle Efficiency principles to solve a quantitative thermodynamics problem.
questions.stem: In a practice exercise, a steam Rankine plant with lead piping adds 2506 kJ per kg in the boiler and rejects 1247 kJ per kg in the condenser. Evaluate the cycle thermal efficiency as a percentage.

options.misconception: Correct application of the principle
Inverted the heat-addition-to-rejection ratio
Reported the rejected-heat fraction as efficiency
Divided net work by the condenser rejection

questions.explanation: Thermal efficiency of any power cycle is net work divided by heat input, which for a Rankine plant is (Qin minus Qout) over Qin. Substituting 2506 and 1247 kJ per kg gives 50.2 percent; the condenser rejection is a necessary loss, not part of the useful output.
questions.hint: Efficiency = (Q_boiler - Q_condenser) / Q_boiler.
